chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no vegetable upon the surface of the earth more noble, nor more beneficial than the Purslane, and it is the vegetable of Fatima (peace be upon her).'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah curse the Clan of Umayya! They named it the 'vegetable of the foolish' out of hatred for us and enmity towards Fatima (peace be upon her).'

key_terms.بَقْلَةَ الْحَمْقَاءِ: The vegetable of the foolish/idiots (disparaging term used by Umayyads)
key_terms.بَقْلَةُ فَاطِمَ: The vegetable of Fatima (a title of honor)

ai.seo_question: Why is Purslane called the vegetable of Fatima and what did the Umayyads say about it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the status of Purslane (Al-Farfakh) by identifying it as the 'vegetable of Fatima,' thereby linking a common dietary staple to the spiritual and physical sustenance of the Ahl al-Bayt. He provides a historical critique of the Umayyad dynasty, explaining that their derogatory label of 'vegetable of the foolish' was a deliberate act of political and sectarian animosity aimed at diminishing the prestige of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her). This narrative underscores the Shia tradition of finding spiritual significance in everyday life and interpreting historical nomenclature through the lens of love for the Prophet's family.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Furat Bin Ahnaf who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no vegetable upon the surface of the earth more noble, nor any more beneficial than the Purslane, and it is a vegetable of Fatima<sup>asws</sup>’. 
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse the Clan of Umayya! They named it as the ‘vegetable of the idiots’ due to their hatred and enmity to Fatima<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Furat ibn Ahnaf who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ’On the face of earth there is no herb more beneficial and graceful than al-Farfakh (purslane) and it is the herb of Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam .’
He (the Imam) then said, ‘May Allah condemn banu ’Umayyah who named it foolish herb due to their animosity toward Fatimah, Alayhi al-Salam.’”
